dial.summary: On August 20, BTC surged 8.1% to $69,581 (total crypto +7.5% to $2.45T, ETH +18%), pulling BTC dominance from 58.94% to 56.8% as altcoins led the breakout — Alt Rotation signals are intensifying but BTC.D has not yet breached the 55% threshold; six of eight indicators remain constructive: 2s10s at +45bps (4-week steepening), DXY at 99.46 (neutral band, 4-week downtrend), stablecoin dominance compressed to 12.6% as capital rotates into risk assets, ISM Manufacturing at 55.6%, Global M2 supportive, Fed Balance Sheet flat/stable; real yields at 2.44% remain the lone structural headwind; PCE (August 26) and Warsh's Jackson Hole keynote (August 28) are the decisive catalysts — dial holds at BTC Accumulation with Alt Rotation transition imminent if BTC.D sustains below 55%.

indicators.name: Global Liquidity (Global M2)
indicators.note: Global 4-bank M2 aggregate (Fed/ECB/BOJ/PBOC) carried at ~$102.7T — July aggregate not yet published (~6-week reporting lag); US M2 confirmed at $23.16T for June 2026, +5.6% YoY (28th consecutive monthly increase, record high per X/@GlobalMktObserv); no YoY contraction signal from any major central bank; 4-week trend up based on sustained US M2 expansion and continued global central bank balance sheet stability; status supportive (4-week uptrend confirmed; YoY contraction headwind condition not triggered).

indicators.name: ISM Manufacturing PMI
indicators.note: July 2026 ISM Manufacturing PMI at 55.6% (released August 3) remains the most recent reading — August 2026 data releases September 1, 2026; sub-indexes: New Orders 56.7%, Production 58.5%, Employment 52.8% (first factory hiring expansion in 18 months), Prices Paid 71.1%; July reading is the highest since May 2022; Philadelphia Fed and Initial Jobless Claims released August 20 provide the first August regional read and labor update (specific values not yet confirmed at time of run); 4-week trend up: June 53.3% → July 55.6% = +2.3pp; status supportive (above 50 and rising; headwind thresholds of <48 falling or >62 not met).

indicators.name: DXY (US Dollar Index)
indicators.note: ICE DXY fell to 99.46 on August 19, 2026 (down 0.20% from 99.64 on August 18; Aug 20 intraday likely similar or slightly lower given risk-on environment with BTC +8.1% and crypto surging); Barchart noted DXY at 99.60 testing rising channel support below declining 200-day MA; 4-week trend down: DXY was ~101.2 around July 19-20 → 99.46 on August 19-20 = approximately -1.7%, above the 0.5% flat threshold; Warsh Jackson Hole keynote August 28 and PCE August 26 are the key directional catalysts; status NEUTRAL (ICE DXY in the 97.5–100 neutral band; below 97.5 would flip to supportive).

indicators.name: Real Yields (US10Y - CPI)
indicators.note: FRED DFII10 at 2.44% as of August 17, 2026 (H.15 released August 18); nominal 10Y Treasury eased to 4.64% on August 20 (from 4.65% August 19, 4.72% August 17), suggesting real yields may have compressed slightly toward ~2.38-2.42% intraday but no official update confirmed yet; the July 23, 2026 10-year TIPS auction cleared at 2.438%, a 16-year high; 4-week trend up: ~2.18% (mid-July) → 2.44% (August 17) = +26bps, well above the 5bps flat threshold; status headwind (above the 2% absolute threshold; soft July PCE August 26 and dovish Warsh keynote August 28 are the catalysts needed to compress real yields below 2%).

indicators.name: 2s10s Yield Curve
indicators.note: August 20, 2026: DGS10 at 4.64% (eased from 4.65% on August 19 and 4.70% on August 18 as risk-on sentiment drove a modest bid for longer duration); DGS2 at 4.19% (latest confirmed August 18); spread = +45bps (narrowed from +51bps due to 10Y easing more than 2Y on the day); 4-week trend up: ~+35bps (mid-July) → +45bps (August 20) = +10bps steepening, above the 5bps flat threshold; status supportive (positive spread AND 4-week steepening trend intact; PCE August 26 and Warsh keynote August 28 are the next directional catalysts; a hawkish Warsh tone could flatten the curve by pushing 2Y higher).

indicators.name: Fed Balance Sheet
indicators.note: WALCL: $6,759,955M ($6.760T) for week ending August 12, 2026 (H.4.1 released August 13); H.4.1 for week ending August 19 released today August 20 at 4:30 PM ET — specific value not yet available at time of run; 4-week trend flat: $6,738,190M (July 29) → $6,759,955M (August 12) = +$21,765M (+0.32%), within the 0.5% flat threshold; status supportive (balance sheet holding at post-2022 stabilization plateau with no aggressive QT signal; reduced September hike probability following NFP shock limits near-term QT acceleration risk).

indicators.name: BTC Funding Rates (perps avg)
indicators.note: CoinGlass blocked by network proxy — value carried forward at +0.004%/8h; BTC surged 8.1% to $69,581 on August 20 (from $64,273 August 19), total crypto market cap $2.45T (+7.5% in 24h), BTC open interest on CoinGlass at $51.9B; intraday funding rates likely moved higher during the 8% pump and may be approaching or exceeding the +0.01%/8h range — users should verify on CoinGlass directly; 30-day trend direction remains down on the carried-forward basis (~+0.006%/8h in late June → +0.004%); status carried as supportive (on the +0.004% basis, below the 0.04%/8h overheating threshold — verify real-time rate against the threshold given today's surge).

indicators.name: Stablecoin Dominance
indicators.note: Stablecoin market cap ~$308B (Aug 13 data; USDT ~$183.4B + USDC + others; price-stable so approximately unchanged intraday) vs. total crypto market cap $2.45T on August 20 (surged from $2.21T on August 19 as BTC +8.1%, ETH +18%, altcoins rallied broadly); stablecoin dominance ~12.6% ($308B / $2,450B), down from 14.0% on August 19 and 14.3% in mid-July; 30-day trend down: ~14.3% (mid-July) → 12.6% (August 20) = -1.7pp compression as capital rotated from stablecoins into risk assets; BTC dominance fell from 58.94% to 56.8% as alts outperformed; status supportive (30-day falling trend confirmed; headwind condition — dominance RISING while TOTAL rises — is the opposite of what is occurring; capital rotation into risk assets accelerating).

upcoming.title: S&P Global Flash PMI (August 2026)
upcoming.note: S&P Global Flash PMI preliminary estimates for August 2026 at 9:45 AM ET — first composite activity read for August; July 2026: Manufacturing 53.8, Services 53.6; the August read is the first broad activity gauge following the NFP shock (−23,000), hot core CPI (3.1%), FOMC Minutes (August 19), and Philly Fed (August 20); with BTC surging 8.1% on August 20 and TOTAL crypto at $2.45T, a stable-to-improving Flash PMI would underpin the BTC Accumulation thesis heading into the PCE/Jackson Hole cluster.

upcoming.title: Consumer Confidence (August 2026)
upcoming.note: Conference Board Consumer Confidence Index for August 2026 at 10:00 AM ET — released the day before the PCE/GDP cluster; incorporates July NFP shock (−23,000), hot core CPI (3.1%), FOMC Minutes tone (August 19), Flash PMI (August 21), and the broad crypto rally (BTC +8% to $69,581 on August 20); a sharp deterioration in confidence would raise Q3 recession risk and bolster the case for September rate cuts; DXY at 99.46 and 2s10s at +45bps already reflect markets tilting toward a hold.

upcoming.title: PCE Price Index (July 2026)
upcoming.note: BEA Personal Income and Outlays at 8:30 AM ET — July PCE Price Index (Fed's preferred inflation gauge), Personal Income, Personal Spending, and Durable Goods Orders; arrives one day before Jackson Hole opens (August 27); hot core CPI (3.1% YoY, August 12) implies core PCE potentially 2.7–2.8% YoY; a reading above 2.8% strongly supports a September hike; a soft print (<2.5%) preserves the rate-cut path, reinforces BTC Accumulation, and would likely push DXY below 97.5 from its current 99.46 neutral level — this is the single most important data print ahead of Jackson Hole.

upcoming.title: GDP 2nd Estimate (Q2 2026)
upcoming.note: BEA releases the second estimate of Q2 2026 GDP at 8:30 AM ET alongside July PCE, one day before Jackson Hole opens; July NFP shock (−23,000) and hot core CPI (3.1%) have raised Q3 recession risk concerns; significant downward revisions alongside soft labor and hot inflation would shift the stagflation narrative from tail risk to baseline, directly setting the tone for Warsh's keynote the following morning.

upcoming.title: Jackson Hole Economic Symposium Opens (August 27–29)
upcoming.note: Kansas City Fed annual Jackson Hole Economic Policy Symposium begins at Jackson Lake Lodge, Wyoming — runs August 27–29; theme: 'Financial Innovation: Implications for Payments and Policy'; by the time proceedings open, markets will have processed PCE (August 26), GDP Q2 2nd estimate (August 26), Consumer Confidence (August 25), and Flash PMI (August 21); Warsh delivers his inaugural Jackson Hole keynote Friday morning August 28; FOMC September 15–16 decision is the next binding commitment after Jackson Hole.

upcoming.title: Initial Jobless Claims (week ended August 22, 2026)
upcoming.note: DOL weekly initial jobless claims at 8:30 AM ET for week ending August 22, 2026 — released the opening morning of Jackson Hole; a sustained rise in claims arriving as Jackson Hole opens would immediately shape the tone for Fed Chair Warsh's inaugural keynote the next morning (August 28).
